text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract is likely to move around 124.00 on Friday, traders said.

They said activity may remain subdued due to a lack of direction ahead of a meeting of the Group of Seven industrialised nations at the weekend, a 10-year JGB auction expected on Tuesday and the release of the Bank of Japan's "tankan" corporate survey on Wednesday.
"The September is likely to consolidate at around 124.00 yen as was seen earlier this week," said a dealer at a securities brokerage.
But he said a downside trial was possible if dealers started to square long positions built in anticipation of a worsening in the results of the tankan survey.
On Thursday, the September eased after Tokyo's close at 124.06 and ended on LIFFE at 123.90. Traders said there was chart support at 123.80, and then at 123.50.

Traders said the fact that the contract's session high had been falling since Tuesday may curb aggressive buying. Thursday's session high was at 124.21 against Tuesday's 124.34. They also said the market was likely to keep an eye on the yen/dollar rate after the yen's decline overnight.
